clues: This city lies on a low inland plain in the south-west of Spain. A river runs through the plain, set between the Atlantic sea and a bigger river.
Snow is almost unknown in this warm southern city. The last snow fell back in 1954, and not one flake has been seen since.
In 1261, the Crown of Castile conquered this city. That one blow ended its time under Moorish rule.
Each May, the great bike racers of the world come to a track just by this city. Their Grand Prix has run there since 1987.
The farms all round this city grow grapes for one famed drink: sherry. That strong wine made the place known far and wide.
